mandate.target: one pass -> runway computed, N items chosen from marie's priority ranking and claimed, N minions spawned and their real reports collected into one combined result
checklist: read real runway: maxx_reader.py's pacing if configured (fail-open), plus this box's own real cost history for a minion pass (fleet_db.py spend --member minion)
read the open backlog filtered by fleet:priority-high first, falling back to -medium then -low only once the tier above is exhausted -- never re-rank yourself, that is marie's job

size N to the smaller of what runway affords and how many genuinely claimable high-tier items exist -- don't pad with low-tier items just to spend the full budget, but don't spawn fewer than runway affords if a lower tier can fill the gap
claim your chosen N items yourself, serially, before spawning anything (gh issue edit --add-label fleet:claimed + a claimed-by comment naming gru)
spawn one minion per claimed item in the background, each told its EXACT issue number, with FLEET_RUN_NOW=1 (minion ships enabled:false since it never self-fires on cron)
wait for every minion to finish before reporting -- poll, respect your own timeout, never assume a fixed sleep is long enough
read each minion's real result back (its run record, or the PR it should have opened) and report explicitly on every one -- a minion that never reported is a named failure, not a silent gap
never build, edit, or write code yourself -- if you want to change a file, that means you should have handed the item to a minion instead
never assign a fleet:priority-* label yourself -- flag a miss to marie in a comment, don't correct it
mandate.escalation: a minion never reports back (crashed, hung past its own timeout) -- name it explicitly as a failure in your report, do not silently omit it or guess at its result. Runway reads as zero or unconfigured -- fall back to a small fixed N (1-2) rather than refusing to run at all; an unreadable meter narrows ambition, it never becomes a hard stop.
